title: Choose the visual world for Veranico
question: The roll assigned Lot Mark. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. This sets type, palette, density and one signature move for the app; the layout (chat beside map, history, quote, approvals) is fixed by the brief.

options.label: Lot Mark
options.lineage: Stencilled export coffee sacks and the cooperative grading room
options.thesis: Every quote is a marked lot: its origin, season and number travel with every figure it produced.
options.viewport: Cobalt top bar with region, language and access state. Chat column on the left with collapsed tool cards. Work area on the right with tabs Map, History, Quote, Approvals; the map opens on the Sul de Minas grid coloured by trigger frequency, legend and season slider below. The insured cell wears a stencilled outline and a manila lot tag carrying the quote id.
options.risk: A stencil face is loud; it must stay on identifiers only, or the working screen turns into packaging.

raised.raise: Every lot tag in the chat is keyed to its evidence: hovering one lights the same cell, bar and quote row in the work area.
One mark burns brightest: only the insured cell and its quote use full-saturation ink, everything else sits a step back.
The season slider remaps the whole grid continuously, with a live readout of year, index value and payout.
Every per-season row sets its figure against one hard right margin, with the running total beneath.

options.label: Zoneamento
options.lineage: Brazil's official agricultural climate-risk zoning sheets (ZARC)
options.thesis: The risk sheet brokers already trust, made live: fixed risk classes on the map and the coverage window drawn as a ribbon of ten-day periods.
options.viewport: Deep teal top bar. Chat on the left, work area on the right. The map shows cells in three fixed risk classes with a ranked legend; above it a 36-cell ribbon of ten-day periods marks the coverage window, and the same ribbon repeats in chat, chart, quote and term sheet.
options.risk: Also where most agricultural dashboards land: it can read as a government GIS portal.

options.label: Cell Specimen
options.thesis: The ERA5 cell is the design unit: the interface is built on a visible construction grid whose module is one map cell.
options.viewport: White shell on faint blue gridlines. Chat left, work area right, every panel edge snapping to the cell module. Trigger frequency and premium are set in monumental grid-built numerals; a grid toggle shows or hides the cell lattice on the map.
options.case: Wins on clarity because the grid is the mechanism itself; loses on identification, since a broker does not see their world in a type specimen.
options.risk: Monumental numerals can crowd a working screen, and white with one accent drifts toward a grey default.

options.label: Course over Terrain
options.lineage: Orienteering maps drawn to the ISOM colour standard
options.thesis: Data is fixed terrain underneath; the insured farm and its active quote ride above in one reserved purple that nothing else may use.
options.viewport: White shell with a narrow legend column. The map carries the cell grid in a fixed ink language; the insured point, its cell and the quote are drawn in purple. The six steps of the flow appear as a numbered course that checks off as the agent completes them.
options.case: Holds clarity for the map and the workflow; loses on identification, because the sport is unfamiliar to this audience.
options.risk: ISOM terrain colours compete with the data ramp on the same map and need strict separation.

options.label: Keyed Rail
options.thesis: Chat and evidence twinned around a narrow rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two columns around a centre rail where each tool call drops a key.
options.case: Serves the provenance proof but not the map, and a scholarly page is far from a broker's desk.
options.risk: Bone paper, serif and vermilion is the look this category of tool defaults to.
options.kept: Every claim keyed to its evidence across the gutter.

options.label: Midnight Diagram
options.thesis: The network as a diagram of disciplined coloured lines.
options.viewport: A dark diagram where the chosen line burns brightest.
options.case: A transit diagram discards geographic distance, and distance is exactly what basis risk is.
options.risk: Dark ground with bright lines reads as a generic climate dashboard.

options.label: Axis Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs a whole grid in real time.
options.viewport: A giant figure and a grid that breathes under a slider.
options.case: The slider-drives-grid interaction fits the season slider, but the world offers little beyond it and no link to the audience.
options.risk: Paper, ink and one accent is a grey screen with a highlight.
options.kept: One control remapping the whole grid, with a live readout.

options.label: Inlay Card
options.thesis: Lists ruled by hand, running times tight to the margin.
options.viewport: A folded sheet of ruled tracklists.
options.case: Handwriting undermines trust in priced figures, and the audience has no tie to it.
options.risk: Reads as novelty on a pricing tool.
options.kept: Figures set tight against one hard right margin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The climate-risk dashboard this category ships, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Dark navy shell, map filling the right side with rounded stat cards over it, chat in a left drawer, teal for every highlight.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other climate and insurance dashboards by design.
